summary.headline: Firstsource Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.9% YoY to INR27.2bn (+2.2% QoQ cc) with EBIT margin 12.4%, but INR717m exceptional charges and a healthcare BPaaS wind-down weigh on outlook.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 22.9% YoY and 5.5% QoQ to INR27.2bn (US$288m), or 12.3% YoY and 2.2% QoQ in constant currency, the ninth straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth. EBIT margin was 12.4%, up 110bps YoY and 20bps QoQ, the seventh straight quarter of margin expansion. Reported PAT was INR1.7bn after INR563m net exceptional charges, against adjusted PAT of INR2.2bn. Management said a healthcare payer BPaaS program is being wound down by a client after a leadership change, costing roughly 1-1.5% of quarterly revenue, and reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10-13% cc growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin.

financial_highlights.change: +22.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ reported; +12.3% YoY, +2.2% QoQ constant currency
three items: INR357m healthcare program termination, INR284m regulatory penalty indemnity, INR76m contingent consideration fair value (Ascensos)

financial_highlights.value: around 23% in Q1; guided 22-24% for FY27

segments.name: BFS
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 14% YoY and 5% QoQ in constant currency; five new logos added. Management cited a strong exit deal pipeline and collections demand from record US consumer debt.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY but fell 2% QoQ in constant currency; four new logos added. Payer-side Medicare Advantage programs were paced by CMS rate changes, and one BPaaS payer program is being wound down.

segments.name: CMT
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 6% YoY and 9% QoQ in constant currency; two new logos added. Management cited volatility from work-packet timing and program transitions in Silicon Valley consumer tech.

segments.name: Diverse portfolio (incl. utilities, Pastdue Credit, retail)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 27% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency; one new logo added. Management said utilities demand is steady with a healthy pipeline.

segments.name: Geography: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 8% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency. Management is setting up sales presence in Canada.

segments.name: Geography: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18% YoY and 6% QoQ in constant currency; two large deals won in Europe. South Africa is the fastest-growing geography, and a Glasgow office was opened.

segments.name: Geography: Australia
segments.commentary: Revenue doubled YoY, driven by both existing clients and new logos.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth reaffirmed at 10% to 13%.
FY27 EBIT margin reaffirmed at 12.25% to 12.75%.
Original guidance had included about 1% to 1.5% of growth from the healthcare BPaaS program now being wound down; management says guidance holds after absorbing this.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be strong as new wins ramp over roughly the next three months.
Long-term aim of a 14% to 15% EBIT margin over the next two to three years, with 50-75bps annual expansion thesis reiterated.
Management expects the exceptional-item amounts (INR357m and INR284m) to be recovered from the client and insurer, though they were expensed on a prudence basis.
capex_capacity: No capex plan, capacity figure or utilisation metric was disclosed on the call.
Headcount 36,875 at Q1 FY27 end, +670 QoQ; offshore and nearshore hiring close to 80% of gross additions.
New delivery footprint: new Glasgow office for UK financial services regulatory work; South Africa cited as fastest-growing geography; Canada sales presence being set up.
Healthcare BPaaS program (payer) wound down; client had been at advanced implementation stage on a new technology platform, now reverting to status quo platform.

Five new growth engines (Middle East, South Africa, Canada and others) and three new capability frontiers (US Retail and CPG practice, marketing services, security and resiliency services) stood up in Q1.
demand_pricing: Four large deals (ACV above US$5m) won in Q1, the sixth straight quarter of four or more; ACV intake was the highest in the last four quarters.
12 new logos added, including three strategic logos; 145 clients above US$1m run-rate; US$5m+ clients up 80% and US$1m+ clients up 45% over two years.
Healthcare deal wins were more than a third of Q1 wins, in line with the roughly one-third revenue share from healthcare.

Hedge book at 30 June 2026: GBP61.6m at an average of 118-120 for the next 12 months; US$119m at about INR92.7/US$. Around 25-30% of the portfolio is in options at roughly 125-130 for GBP; blended GBP rate about 123-124 and USD about 94.
Management said the BPaaS client is wound down by client decision after leadership change, and the client has added more work elsewhere in the account.

qa_highlights.question: What was the revenue impact of the healthcare BPaaS termination in Q1, and what does the INR271m charge include?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the Q1 revenue impact of about 1-1.5%. The charge relates to partner-ecosystem deliverables; Firstsource is the single point of contact and is recovering amounts from the client and repaying partners.

qa_highlights.question: How is guidance maintained despite this hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was the best quarter for new deal wins in the last four quarters and that several wins ramp quickly, offsetting the 1-1.5% loss, so the 10-13% range is retained.

qa_highlights.question: Is the healthcare payer churn a sector-wide issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it an isolated, one-off event caused by a new client leader pausing programs, not a secular trend. The same client continues to expand its footprint.

qa_highlights.question: How does the wound-down program compare with the USD50m steady-state run-rate expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 1-1.5% contribution was its estimate at the start of the year, reflecting slower ramp and schedule risk; the program will not reach the implied trajectory this fiscal year.

qa_highlights.question: How are segment margins evolving versus FY24 (BFS above 20% now, healthcare low double-digit)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly segment movements are aberrations from ramp costs and that company margin is up from 11% eight quarters ago to 12.4%, with no systemic issue seen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedge liability and forward book outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the GBP book is typically 50-75% of committed year-one value and USD about 25%; GBP 61.6m and USD 119m are hedged for the next 12 months at blended rates of about 123-124 (GBP) and 94 (USD).

risks_watch: Healthcare payer exposure: Medicare Advantage program pacing under CMS rate changes, with healthcare Q1 revenue down 2% QoQ cc; management attributed this to pacing, not demand.

Recovery of INR357m (healthcare program termination) and INR284m (regulatory penalty indemnity, insurance claim) exceptional charges; both expensed on a prudence basis, with recovery timing not committed.
Ramp of new wins: management expects H2 FY27 to be strong, but wins are phased transformational deals, so revenue conversion timing is uncertain.
Guidance hold at 10-13% cc growth and 12.25-12.75% EBIT margin after absorbing the 1-1.5% BPaaS loss; watch whether the lower end is still tracking next quarter.
Europe and CMT volatility: Europe shift to offshore and nearshore, and CMT timing of work packets and Silicon Valley consumer tech program transitions; voluntary attrition at 27.5%.
Hedge book: GBP61.6m at 118-120 and US$119m at about INR92.7/US$ for the next 12 months; option cover on 25-30% of the portfolio; watch INR-GBP and INR-USD rate moves on margins.
key_quotes: Importantly, because this engagement was still in the early phase of its ramp and had not reached its steady -state run rate, the impact of this on our reported revenue is limited.
So, I would think of it as , this is a very isolated, one-off instance that ends up happening and primarily because, as I said, they had a leadership change.
We do expect the second half of the year to be strong, but at the same time, I think, it's broadly going to be in line with our ability to hit the guidance that we've reinforced.
I wouldn't read too much into one quarter over the other. These are standard aberrations that would happen.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year guidance, the deal pipeline and the client relationships, and firm that the healthcare charges are one-off. Cautious and somewhat defensive on the segment margin questions and on the healthcare BPaaS ramp, where it gave no quantified forward segment margin path and said the program would not reach the implied trajectory this fiscal year.

adds.what: New Glasgow office for UK financial services regulatory work

growth.why: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth of 10-13% (midpoint 11.5%) was reaffirmed even after absorbing a ~1-1.5% of revenue drag from the healthcare BPaaS wind-down, backed by four large deals (ACV above US$5m), 12 new logos and a strong Q1 deal intake, though no specific capacity or contract-value figures were quantified for the full-year number.
